gibraltar.title: Flag of Gibraltar

colors.note: The upper field representing the white walls of the fortress.
The lower field representing the bloodshed in defence of the Rock.

desc:
- A white field over a red field in a 2:1 ratio, with a three-towered red castle and a golden key hanging from the gate
- One of the oldest flags in the world, granted by Royal Warrant of Queen Isabella I of Castile in 1502
- **Construction:** the flag is divided horizontally in a 2:1 ratio — white (top two-thirds) over red (bottom one-third)
- A red three-towered castle is centred on the white band, with a gold key hanging from the castle gate into the red band
trivia:
- Gibraltar's flag reflects the contested status between Britain and Spain
- The white and red castle (fortress) represents the Rock of Gibraltar
- Gibraltar uses the Union Jack as its official flag but has a unique local flag for unofficial use
